set.typical_award_size: No standing County land program. Known actions: (1) Gianone Park remnant, APN 143-110-05, about four undeveloped acres at the north end of the 15.02-acre County parcel at 2885 E. Harding Way, Stockton (appraised September 8, 2023 at $930,000 assuming R-H zoning; currently zoned P-F). The Board declared it exempt surplus on November 12, 2024 (R-24-207) for the sole purpose of affordable housing, with no minimum bid and an as-is sale; the January 14, 2025 bid opening was continued to a date uncertain (B-25-28) after the Board signaled a desire to prioritize park funding, and County Counsel restated that the property was declared surplus for affordable housing. Sale proceeds would go to the Parks Development Fund. A follow-up Surplus Land Act notice of availability (sale or long-term ground lease, offers due January 30, 2026) appears only on procurement aggregators. (2) Victory Gardens, 49 HACSJ units for homeless veterans built on 2.5 acres of County-owned land in French Camp under a County ground lease, completed fall 2022. (3) The French Camp Veterans Village (about 150 tiny homes, WellNest Group with the Veterans Services Office, $38.5 million Homekey+ request authorized July 29, 2025) is not on County land: WellNest secured 16.5 acres near the VA clinic and Homekey+ funds would buy the land.
set.affordability_requirement: Gianone Park: the Board declared the site surplus solely for affordable housing. Surplus Land Act priority for developers with at least 25% of units at or below 80% AMI (Government Code 54222.5) or deeper restrictions negotiated with the County. Victory Gardens: HUD-VASH and Housing Choice Voucher households.
set.next_deadline: No open round as of November 10, 2026. The Gianone Park bid opening was continued to a date uncertain on January 14, 2025 and the later notice of availability closed January 30, 2026; no Board award of the site appears on 2025 or 2026 Board agendas. Watch Board agendas (sanjoaquincountyca.iqm2.com) and the HCD surplus land notices map.
set.layering_notes: San Joaquin County has no county housing trust fund, no county housing bond and no inclusionary ordinance; the County's own capital for multifamily is limited to HUD pass-through funds administered by the Human Services Agency Neighborhood Preservation Division (sjchsa.org), while the regional gap lender is the SJCOG-sponsored San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund and the main voucher and development partner is the Housing Authority of the County of San Joaquin (HACSJ). County land is the most likely form of County contribution to a new deal: Victory Gardens combined a County ground lease with VHHP ($6.8 million), tax credits ($19.6 million), County HOME, CESH and CDBG. The Gianone Park site is zoned P-F and would need a rezone; Board members have shown interest in park use of proceeds, so confirm Board direction with General Services before pursuing it.
eligible_project_detail: ground lease or sale of surplus County land
set.audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: Gianone Park facts confirmed on the January 14, 2025 Board item (iqm2 LegiFile 11944: board letter, B-25-28 and draft resolution); Victory Gardens County land and ground lease confirmed on hacsj.org; corrected the French Camp Veterans Village, which the July 29, 2025 board letter (LegiFile 12476) shows is on land WellNest secured, not County land, with the Homekey+ application authorized in 2025. The November 2025 notice of availability itself is still seen only on aggregators.

set.layering_notes: This is the only locally generated housing fund in South Lake Tahoe. Multifamily rental projects are exempt from both the unit requirement and the fee (chapter text on the gocodebook mirror), so apartment developers owe nothing; the fund is fed by large single-family and condo construction, which is the dominant product in the Basin. Spending the Workforce Housing Fund is at Council discretion with no NOFA or guidelines published; pair requests with the City's HOME program income, PLHA formula and Prohousing Incentive Program dollars (see the City direct financing record) and with the County Affordable Housing Trust Fund, County PLHA and County HOME/CDBG records, which also have no standing NOFA. The ordinance grew out of Housing Element Program 2-11 (2022 to 2027 cycle) and the January 2023 Analysis of Local Funding Sources. Adoption date conflict: the August 2026 draft Housing Element says Council adopted the ordinance in December 2024, but the March 26, 2024 Master Fee Schedule already lists the inclusionary fee tiers, so the fee was in place by early 2024. Fee amounts are confirmed on the official Master Fee Schedule; unit percentages and exemptions were read on the gocodebook mirror because codepublishing.com returns 403.

set.typical_award_size: Regulatory incentive, not a subsidy. Lincoln does have a local density bonus chapter: Municipal Code Chapter 18.59, Density Increase and Incentive Program (Ord. 881B, April 23, 2013, replacing a 1995 chapter). It applies in all zones allowing residential use and grants qualifying projects and land transfers a density bonus, incentives and concessions in the amounts specified in Government Code 65915 et seq., as amended, so current state tiers apply (20% to 50% bonuses, 80% for 100% affordable projects, up to four concessions, parking caps). The Housing Element (Action 2.3) identifies Section 18.59 as the City's density bonus provision; Action 2.5 also lists a 35% bonus for market-rate rental projects with 20% low or 10% very low income units, a figure superseded by state law.
set.affordability_requirement: State thresholds (5% very low, 10% lower, 10% moderate for-sale, senior housing, 100% affordable); the City and applicant agree on a method to ensure continued availability of the bonus units before approval (18.59.060), with 55-year rental covenants under state law.
set.next_deadline: Processed with entitlements; application filed in writing with the Planning Division concurrently with other entitlements (18.59.050). No deadline.
set.layering_notes: No local enhancements beyond state law, and no local trust fund, fee waiver ordinance, inclusionary fund or city NOFA in Lincoln beyond the negotiated Housing Element incentives (record above) and CDBG. Chapter 18.59 incorporates Government Code 65915 by reference, so it tracks state amendments automatically. Chapter text was read on the zoneomics mirror (the official host, municode, returns 403); the City's Housing Element confirms that Section 18.59 is the density bonus provision.
set.audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: corrected the earlier finding that Lincoln has no density bonus chapter. Chapter 18.59 (Density Increase and Incentive Program, Ord. 881B, 2013) appears in the zoneomics Title 18 mirror (chapter_6 page) and is cited as the density bonus section in Housing Element Action 2.3 on the City-hosted Housing Element PDF. Municode remains blocked.

reason: Lincoln Municipal Code Chapter 18.59 is a local density bonus chapter incorporating Government Code 65915, contrary to the record's statement that none exists.
